label: <DEL> step of longer sequences (+ late first-occurrence d/t/u/w/r/p/k/2 inputs)
explanation: Mostly a delimiter unit: 81% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (active on 47% of delimiter steps). How often it fires there goes up with sequence length (L=3 to L=9) and with the first original token, i.e. the first token to be output. It is strongest when the first token is g, b, a, q, l or e and weaker for later letters like u, v, d or w. The remaining ~19% of mass sits in the last few original-phase steps (t >= 6) of long sequences, on first occurrences of particular tokens (2, d, t, u, w, r, p, k), and often builds up over the steps just before <DEL>. It is essentially silent at t < 3 and in the copy phase (0.1% of mass). Precision is limited because many delimiter steps, especially short sequences or late-alphabet first tokens, stay below threshold.
